name: launch_app
description: Start a Java Swing application with the swing2mcp agent injected and connect to it. `command` is a shell command line, e.g. `java -jar app.jar` or a start script; the agent is added through JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, so the application itself is not changed. Application output goes to a log file. Returns once the agent is up, usually before the first window: call wait_for next.

command.description: Shell command that starts the application

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the agent (default 60)

name: list_apps
description: List running Java applications. Those with the swing2mcp agent show their windows; the connected one is marked with *. The others can be connected with connect_app, which loads the agent into them without restarting.

name: connect_app
description: Connect to a running Java application by pid (see list_apps). If it was started without swing2mcp, the agent is loaded into it first: no restart, and the application keeps its state (open windows, logged-in user). Works with Java 8+ processes of the same OS user.

name: stop_app
description: Kill an application: ends its process and child processes at once, without asking it to close, so unsaved work is lost and no "save changes?" dialog appears. To exit normally, use the application's own exit menu or close button instead. Only applications with the swing2mcp agent can be stopped (see list_apps). Default: the connected application.

pid.description: Process id from list_apps. Default: the connected application

name: snapshot
description: Describe what is on screen: every visible window as an indented outline of components (role, label, value, state) with a [ref=eN] for each element. Use refs with click, type_text, select_option and screenshot. Refs stay valid while the component exists. `field=` is the Java field holding the component, `class=` an application class. Prefer this over screenshot; use screenshot for custom-painted parts and layout.

window.description: Ref of a single window to describe

maxRows.description: Rows/items listed per table or list (default 10; trees twice that). read_items reads the rest

expandMenus.description: Also list items of closed menus

name: screenshot
description: PNG image of a window or component, painted by Swing itself (works even if the window is covered). Without ref: the modal dialog, active window or main frame.

name: click
description: Click a component like a user would, with real mouse events (the mouse moves to the point, then presses and releases): a focusable component takes the focus first (so the previous field's input verifier and focus-lost handlers run). Menu items, even inside closed menus, are activated directly. For tables, lists and trees pass `value` (the cell's text, the item's text, or a tree path like "Root/Child") or `row` (and `col` for tables). Use clickCount=2 for double-click, button=right for context menus, modifiers="Ctrl" or "Shift" to add to or extend the selection (select_option with values/indexes does several at once). The click goes to that point of the window as a real one does: a component that is scrolled out of view is scrolled into view first, a click on a label inside a clickable panel reaches the panel, and if something else lies on top of the component there the click is refused and the error says what covers it. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

value.description: Table: text of a cell to click (first match; limit with col). List: item text. Tree: node path, ancestors get expanded

header.description: Table: click the header of column col (e.g. to sort)

modifiers.description: Keys held during the click: Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Meta, or combined like Ctrl+Shift

dialog.description: Answer the modal dialog this action opens with this button (text, or ok/yes/no/cancel); its message is reported. An error if no dialog opens within 3 s

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: hover
description: Move the mouse over a component without pressing a button, like a user who points at it: the application gets real mouse-entered and mouse-moved events, so what it does when pointed at happens (a rollover, a menu or panel that opens on hover, a shape that follows the mouse). The point is the component's center, x/y inside it, or an item by value or row/col as in click. click and drag move the mouse to their own point first, so hover is only for pointing without clicking. With `wheel` the mouse wheel is turned there as well, to scroll or to zoom what is under the mouse. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

value.description: Table cell text, list item text or tree path to point at

row.description: Row (table/tree) or index (list) to point at

wheel.description: Turn the mouse wheel this many notches at that point: positive is down (toward the user), negative is up

modifiers.description: Keys held meanwhile, e.g. Ctrl for a zoom that asks for Ctrl+wheel

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: type_text
description: Type into a text field, text area, password field, spinner or editable combo box like a user: the field gets the focus (the previous field's input verifier runs; if it refuses, nothing is typed and the result says why), the old text is selected and each character is sent as real key events, so key listeners, document filters and formatters run. Replaces the content unless append=true; submit=true then presses Enter. "\n" types Enter and "\t" types Tab (moves to the next field). Formatted fields and spinners commit on Enter or when the focus leaves them. The application window does not need to be in front. mode=set sets the text directly without key events (faster, but skips key listeners). Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

append.description: Keep the current text and type at its end

mode.description: keys (default): key events inside the application; set: set the text directly; os: real keyboard through the operating system (brings the window to the front; rarely needed)

dialog.description: Answer the modal dialog this action opens with this button (text, or ok/yes/no/cancel); its message is reported. An error if no dialog opens within 3 s

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: press_key
description: Press keys like a user: "Enter", "Escape", "Tab", "Shift+Tab", "Up", "F5", "Ctrl+S", "Alt+F4", or several separated by spaces ("Tab Tab Enter"). Keys go to the component that has the keyboard focus (marked "focused" in the snapshot), or to ref after focusing it, so key bindings, menu shortcuts, the default button and focus traversal work as for a user. Without ref, keys go to the open modal dialog if there is one. The application window does not need to be in front. The result says where the focus is afterwards. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

key.description: Key or chord, e.g. Enter, Escape, Ctrl+S, Shift+Tab, F2; several separated by spaces

ref.description: Component to focus first (default: the focused component)

mode.description: keys (default): key events inside the application; os: real keyboard through the operating system (brings the window to the front)

dialog.description: Answer the modal dialog this action opens with this button (text, or ok/yes/no/cancel); its message is reported. An error if no dialog opens within 3 s

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: select_option
description: Select an entry by visible text (`value`) or position (`index`) in a combo box, list, tab pane, table or tree. Table: value is the text of any cell of the row (limit it to a column with col); the cell is selected as by a click. Tree: value is a path like "Root/Child/Leaf" (the root may be left out; " > " also separates); ancestors are expanded on the way, as a user would. Several entries of a list, table or tree: `values` or `indexes` (ranges like "2-5"), or a range from value/index `to` another; they are selected with real clicks, the first plain, the others with Ctrl, a range's end with Shift. add=true keeps the current selection; deselect=true Ctrl-clicks the given entries that are selected. The result lists what is selected afterwards. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

index.description: Position; for tables the row, for trees the visible row

values.description: Several entries by text (table: a cell's text; tree: paths)

indexes.description: Several positions and ranges, e.g. 0,2,5-8 (table rows, list items, visible tree rows)

to.description: End of a range that starts at value (text) or index (number)

add.description: Keep the current selection and add to it (Ctrl)

deselect.description: Remove the given entries from the selection (Ctrl-click the selected ones)

col.description: Table column to search in or select

dialog.description: Answer the modal dialog this action opens with this button (text, or ok/yes/no/cancel); its message is reported. An error if no dialog opens within 3 s

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: select_menu
description: Choose a menu item like a user: path such as "File > Export > PDF" in the window's menu bar. Menus are opened level by level, so code that fills or enables items when a menu opens runs; a disabled item is reported, not clicked. A path ending at a menu leaves it open. With context=true, ref is right-clicked and the path is chosen in the context menu that opens (without ref: in the context menu already open). ref without context picks the menu bar of that component's window or internal frame. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

path.description: Menu texts separated by >, e.g. File > Open

ref.description: Component to right-click (context=true), or one inside the window whose menu bar to use

context.description: Use the context (right-click) menu of ref

dialog.description: Answer the modal dialog this action opens with this button (text, or ok/yes/no/cancel); its message is reported. An error if no dialog opens within 3 s

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: drag
description: Drag with the mouse like a user: press at the start, move, release at the end. The start is ref (an item by value/row/col, a slider's thumb, a split pane's divider, x/y, or its center; edge=right starts at a cell's or header column's right border, e.g. to resize a column). The end is dx/dy from the start, or toRef with toValue (item text or tree path; a number for a slider value or divider location), toRow/toCol, at=before/on/after, or toX/toY. mode=auto (default) picks: mouse - real mouse events inside the application (pan a map or canvas, move a slider, a divider, a table column; window may be in the background); transfer - drag and drop between components through the application's TransferHandlers (lists, tables, trees, text, drop zones): the source's data is dropped on the target at a real drop location, canImport/importData and the source's exportDone run as for a user, without the operating system's drag and drop; picked for drag-enabled sources; os - the real mouse pointer (window comes to the front; only for drag and drop that needs the operating system). The result says what changed (slider value, divider, column widths, a custom component's picture) or what the drop did. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

ref.description: Component to start the drag in

value.description: Start on this item (list item text, table cell text, tree path)

header.description: Table: start on the header of column col (move or, with edge=right, resize it)

edge.description: Start at this border of the item or header column

dx.description: Move this far right (negative: left) from the start

dy.description: Move this far down (negative: up) from the start

toRef.description: Component to drop on or drag to (default: ref)

toValue.description: Target item text or tree path; a number for a slider value or split pane divider location

toRow.description: Target row/item; the row count means after the last one

toHeader.description: Table: the end is on toRef's header (column toCol)

at.description: Where on the target item to drop (default on)

action.description: Drag and drop action (default: move if the source allows it; Ctrl means copy)

modifiers.description: Keys held during the drag, e.g. Ctrl, Shift

steps.description: Number of mouse moves (default about one per 12 px)

durationMs.description: How long the moves take (default 300; os 500)

dialog.description: Answer the modal dialog this action opens with this button (text, or ok/yes/no/cancel); its message is reported. An error if no dialog opens within 3 s

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: handle_dialog
description: Answer a dialog like a user: press one of its buttons by text or by role (ok, yes, no, cancel; open/save in file choosers; these work in any UI language), "close" for the window's close box. `text` first types the answer of an input dialog (or picks it in its combo box); `path` first puts a file or directory path into a file chooser and, unless button says otherwise, presses its Open/Save button. Without ref: the open modal dialog (or the newest dialog). The result repeats the dialog's title and message. To answer a dialog that an action will open, pass dialog=<button> to that action instead. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

button.description: Button text, or ok/yes/no/cancel/open/save, or close

path.description: File or directory for a file chooser

ref.description: The dialog (or any component in it); default: the open modal dialog

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: read_items
description: Read the contents of a table, list, tree or combo box, page by page, as the user sees them (the text the cells show, with the underlying value where it reads differently). The snapshot shows only the first rows. Table: rows from `start` (view order, as sorted/filtered on screen), optionally only some `columns`. Tree: without path, the visible rows; with `path`, that node and its descendants down to `depth` levels, read from the tree model without expanding anything (trees that load children on expand need expand_node first). `find` keeps only entries containing that text.

start.description: First row/item to return (default 0); with find in a table, list or combo: matches to skip

columns.description: Table: column names or indexes, comma-separated

depth.description: Tree with path: levels below the node (default 1)

name: expand_node
description: Expand (or collapse) a tree node given by its path, like clicking its toggle: ancestors are expanded on the way and expansion listeners run, so trees that load children on expand fill in. Says if the application vetoed it. Waits first (up to timeoutMs) until the component is visible, enabled, editable where needed, and not blocked by a modal dialog or busy overlay, so no wait_for is needed for a component that is about to become usable. Returns the new snapshot.

path.description: Node path like Root/Child (the root may be left out)

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the component to become usable (default 10000)

name: wait_for
description: Wait until `text` appears anywhere in the snapshot (or disappears with gone=true). Without text, waits for the first window to appear, which is useful right after launch_app. Returns the snapshot; a timeout is an error, with the snapshot at that moment.

name: hot_reload
description: Apply code changes to the running application without restarting it. Workflow: edit the Java sources, compile them (e.g. `mvn -q compile` in the application's module, or let the IDE build), then call hot_reload. Changed classes are found in the class directories (target/classes) and loaded into the running JVM. If only event handlers, painting or business logic changed, open screens keep their state; if a screen's construction code changed (constructor, initComponents, @PostConstruct...), that screen is rebuilt. Changes that add or remove methods or fields (including new lambdas) cannot be applied on a standard JVM: the result explains which, and nothing is changed; then restart the application. Only classes whose code really changed are reloaded, even if the build rewrote all class files. In a multi-module project, a module that the application runs from its jar needs classesDir (or start the application with mvn swing2mcp:run -Dswing2mcp.classesDirs=...). Returns the new snapshot.

classesDir.description: Directory with compiled classes, if the application was not started from it (e.g. a module that runs from its jar)

rebuild.description: auto (default): rebuild screens whose construction code changed; all: rebuild every open screen of a reloaded class; none: never

refs.description: Refs of screens to rebuild in any case

name: spring_beans
description: For Spring applications: list the beans of the application's Spring context, which is found automatically without any change to the application. Window and panel beans are listed first and can be shown with open_spring_bean. Fails politely if the application has no Spring.

filter.description: Only beans whose name or class contains this text

name: open_spring_bean
description: For Spring applications: show a window or panel bean directly instead of navigating menus. Windows and dialogs are opened (prototype beans give a fresh instance); a panel that is not on screen yet is shown in a new frame; a panel in a hidden tab gets its tab selected. Returns the new snapshot.
